response:
## 1) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Skipped prom-rule abilities still grant Duplicate, enabling it for non-Grafana rules

Affected:
- public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:287-334
- public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:397-406
- public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:73-92

Explanation:
When `skipToken` is passed, `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined)` still builds a full abilities map:
- `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` returns `loading: false`.
- So `MaybeSupported` is `AlwaysSupported`.
- `isPluginProvided` is false, so `duplicateSupported` is `AlwaysSupported`.
- `Duplicate` therefore becomes `toAbility(AlwaysSupported, rulesPermissions.create)` with the *Grafana* create permission.

`AlertRuleMenu` combines the results with OR: `canDuplicate = rulerDuplicate || grafanaDuplicate`. For cloud/Mimir rules, the prom path is skipped, yet any user with Grafana `alert.rules:create` gets Duplicate. This happens even when the ruler-based check denies it, for example for plugin-provided rules or when the user lacks datasource rule permissions. `Explore` is also reported as supported for a skipped rule.

A skipped rule should yield `NotSupported` for every action.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const abilities = useMemo<Abilities<AlertRuleAction>>(() => {
  if (!rule) {
    return mapValues(AlertRuleAction, () => [NotSupported, false]) as Abilities<AlertRuleAction>;
  }
  // ... existing logic
}, [...]);
~~~

## 2) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Federated rule groups no longer treated as immutable in legacy hook

Affected:
- public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:222-248

Explanation:
`useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule: CombinedRule)` used to compute `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`. It now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, which hardcodes `isFederated = false`.

As a result, every consumer of the deprecated `CombinedRule`-based hook (the legacy list, the rule viewer, and others) will now offer Edit, Delete and Pause for Mimir federated rule groups. Those groups were previously blocked as immutable. This is a silent behavioral regression.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
export function useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule: CombinedRule): Abilities<AlertRuleAction> {
  const groupIdentifierV2 = useMemo(() => groupIdentifier.fromCombinedRule(rule), [rule]);
  const abilities = useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2);
  const isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group);
  return useMemo(() => (isFederated ? applyImmutable(abilities) : abilities), [abilities, isFederated]);
}
~~~
Alternatively, pass a federation flag into `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`.

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Missing React `key` on GrafanaRuleListItem in list rendering

Affected:
- public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/FilterView.tsx:157-162

Explanation:
The previous `GrafanaRuleLoader` element had `key={key}`. The replacement `GrafanaRuleListItem` drops it while still being rendered inside a `.map`.

This causes React key warnings. It can also cause incorrect reconciliation as the filtered results stream in or change: state and hooks get reused across different rules, and items are remounted unnecessarily.

Proposed fix:
~~~tsx
<GrafanaRuleListItem
  key={key}
  rule={rule}
  groupIdentifier={groupIdentifier}
  namespaceName={ruleWithOrigin.namespaceName}
  showLocation={true}
/>
~~~

## 4) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Pause/Restore/Export/DeletePermanently restricted to alerting rules, excluding Grafana recording rules

Affected:
- public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:301-330

Explanation:
In the ruler-based hook, these actions were gated on `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule = rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`. That check is true for both alerting and recording Grafana rules.

The new prom-based hook gates them on `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`. Grafana-managed recording rules therefore lose Pause, Restore, Export and DeletePermanently in the new list view.

The comment "All GrafanaPromRuleDTO rules are Grafana-managed by definition" suggests the intent was the broader check. Only Silence should be alerting-only.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const isGrafanaManagedRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule);
const isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule);
...
[AlertRuleAction.Silence]: [silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule],
[AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport]: [isGrafanaManagedRule, exportAllowed],
[AlertRuleAction.Pause]: [MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable && isGrafanaManagedRule, isEditable ?? false],
[AlertRuleAction.Restore]: [MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable && isGrafanaManagedRule, isEditable ?? false],
[AlertRuleAction.DeletePermanently]: [MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable && isGrafanaManagedRule, (isRemovable && isAdmin()) ?? false],
~~~

## 5) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Title: Rule view link lost `returnTo` parameter

Affected:
- public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:40

Explanation:
The deleted implementation built the href as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })`. The new component drops `returnTo`.

As a result, navigating from the list to a rule and back no longer preserves the list's filters and location. This is a UX regression unrelated to removing the ruler API.

Proposed fix:
~~~tsx
const returnTo = createReturnTo();
...
href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo }),
~~~

## 6) Severity: LOW | Type: Performance
Title: `logWarning` invoked during render on every re-render

Affected:
- public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/components/RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:66-70
- public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/components/RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:146

Explanation:
`getEditableIdentifier` runs in the render path and calls `logWarning` whenever an identifier can't be built. Because the list polls on an interval and re-renders frequently, this will repeatedly emit analytics warnings for the same rule.

The early `return null` also comes after some hooks. Any hooks declared later in the component, which this diff does not show, would violate the Rules of Hooks; please verify.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const identifier = useMemo(() => getEditableIdentifier(groupIdentifier, rule, promRule), [groupIdentifier, rule, promRule]);
useEffect(() => {
  if (!identifier) {
    logWarning('Unable to construct an editable rule identifier');
  }
}, [identifier]);
~~~

true_positives.golden_comment: The rendered GrafanaRuleListItem is missing the required key prop for React list items. This can cause rendering issues when the list order changes.
true_positives.matched_candidate: Missing React key on GrafanaRuleListItem in list rendering - the replacement component drops the key prop while being rendered inside a .map, causing React key warnings and incorrect reconciliation
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies exactly the same problem as the golden comment: the GrafanaRuleListItem component is missing the required React key prop when rendered in a list (.map). Both comments point out that this causes rendering/reconciliation issues. The candidate even provides additional detail about React key warnings and incorrect reconciliation, which aligns with the golden comment's mention of 'rendering issues when the list order changes'.

false_negatives.golden_comment: RuleActionsButtons is invoked with only promRule, but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer inside RuleActionsButtons still depends on a Grafana Ruler rule being present, so for Grafana rules coming from list views the 'Silence notifications' menu entry (now driven by Grafana Prom abilities) will toggle showSilenceDrawer without ever rendering the drawer. This means clicking 'Silence notifications' for these rules has no visible effect, even when abilities indicate silencing is allowed.
